target: BCEAO national directors (Senegal, Ivory Coast, Benin, Burkina Faso, Guinea-Bissau, Mali, Niger, Togo)
searched: Searched for the BCEAO national directors listing in French and English; fetched https://ns2.bceao.int/en/content/board-directors; searched for 'directeur national BCEAO biographie carriere banque commerciale'; fetched the news biography of the new Togo national director (beninwebtv.com) and of Vice Governor Mamadou Diop (wakatsera.com).
outcome: There is no BCEAO page that lists its eight national directors with careers. The Board of Directors page names only Governor Jean Claude Kassi Brou and otherwise describes the board by formula ('a member appointed by each of the Governments'), with no biographies. The Togo national director Ekoue Djro Glokpor's only stated employer is the BCEAO itself (Director of Accounting, General Director of Organization and Information Systems, Advisor to the Governor), no dates, no private firm. Vice Governor Mamadou Diop (Niger) is reported to have begun his career at 'l'ancienne BIAO' before joining the BCEAO in the late 1970s, then national director of the Niamey agency from 1984, headquarters roles from 1997, retirement 2009, Vice Governor 2011-2018 and again from 29 April 2021. The article never says what BIAO was, so under the precedent on unstated ownership this cannot be filed. No record for any of the eight countries.
next_step: For Diop: a BCEAO or BIAO source stating that the Banque Internationale pour l'Afrique Occidentale was a private commercial bank, and giving his role and dates there - the BCEAO's own 'Annuaire des Banques, etablissements financiers a caractere bancaire et compagnies financieres de l'UMOA' series, or a BCEAO press release announcing his appointment with a full CV. For the national directors generally: the BCEAO annual report's organigramme PDFs name the directors but not their careers; each state's official gazette appointment decree would be the document.

target: BEAC (Cameroon, Central African Republic, Chad, Congo, Equatorial Guinea, Gabon)

target: Solomon Islands - Central Bank of Solomon Islands board
searched: Searched for the CBSI board of directors; fetched https://www.cbsi.com.sb/about-us/our-organisation/board-directors.
outcome: Full careers are given for every director, which makes this the most detailed Pacific board page found, but no employer is characterised. The finance-sector items are: board member David K.C. Quan listed as former Deputy Chairman of the National Bank of Solomon Islands and former Chairman of the Solomon Islands National Provident Fund (a statutory pension body, public), and Deputy Governor Raynold Moveni with the Development Bank of Solomon Islands (Research and Marketing Officer 1997, Senior Research and Development Officer January to October 1998) and the IMF (Advisor to the Executive Director, Washington DC, September 2007 to October 2009). The page states ownership for none of them. The National Bank of Solomon Islands has a government-sounding name and no stated ownership, which is exactly the situation the ECCB precedent says not to file; a development bank is public by the stated rule; the IMF role would be a public_move but belongs to a career inside the central bank rather than a move to or from private finance. Nothing filed. Mr Quan's other firms - Quan Chee Corporation Limited, AVIS Solomon Islands, Solomon Telekom - are not finance.
next_step: A source stating the ownership of the National Bank of Solomon Islands during Mr Quan's deputy chairmanship, and the dates of that role: the CBSI Annual Report's licensed-institutions list, or the bank's own or its parent's corporate history. CBSI Annual Report 2024 at https://www.cbsi.com.sb/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/CBSI-Annual-Report-2024.pdf is the place to start.

target: Vanuatu - Reserve Bank of Vanuatu board
searched: Searched for the RBV board; fetched https://rbv.gov.vu/index.php/en/about/board-of-directors/current-board-members.
outcome: Four members with careers: Chairman Andrew Kauisiama (RBV Governor 1998-2003 and earlier RBV research roles, Office of the Prime Minister, Ministries of Trade and Finance, University of the South Pacific, and boards of Air Vanuatu, Vanuatu Terminal Services, National Housing Corporation), Governor August Letlet (RBV, and Director General of the Ministry of Finance and Economic Management), Nikunj Soni (EU programme team lead, Timor-Leste Ministry of Finance, PNG-Australia Governance Facility, UK FCDO, Pacific Institute of Public Policy) and Dr Gregoire Nimbtik (Melanesian Spearhead Group, Office of the Prime Minister). Every employer is a government body, a central bank, a university or an aid programme. No private finance anywhere. Closed with nothing.
next_step: None needed for the current board. If later rounds want Vanuatu, the previous-board-members pages on the same site (rbv.gov.vu/index.php/en/about/board-of-directors/previous-board-members) carry biographies of past directors.

target: Taiwan - Mega Financial Holding / Mega International Commercial Bank seat
searched: Fetched the Central Bank of the Republic of China's official 21st Board curriculum-vitae table at https://www.cbc.gov.tw/tw/dl-213961-b30b4e8258b545c987ca1bc693c1f11d.html after two other attachment URLs returned binary data.
outcome: The table lists standing director 董瑞斌 (Dong Jui-pin) with his current occupation as Chairman of Mega Financial Holding Co., Ltd. and Mega International Commercial Bank Co., Ltd. This is a sitting central bank director concurrently chairing a commercial bank, but it is not filed: the brief's own caution is that Taiwan's largest banks are government-controlled, and the Ministry of Finance is widely understood to be Mega's largest shareholder. The CBC table states nothing about ownership, so under the unstated-ownership precedent it settles nothing in either direction. A record here would be wrong if Mega is state-controlled.
next_step: Mega Financial Holding's own annual report or its Taiwan Stock Exchange MOPS filing, section on major shareholders - if the Ministry of Finance or state banks hold a controlling block, Mega is public and the seat is not a revolving-door record; if not, it is one, and the CBC table already supplies the role and the 27 January 2025 to 26 January 2030 term.

searched: Fetched Bank SinoPac's own corporate profile at https://bank.sinopac.com/sinopacbt/en/about/20180102153120459000000000000958.html and the Caproasia merger article of 31 March 2026.
outcome: Bank SinoPac's own profile gives inception 28 January 1992 and confirms it is a wholly owned subsidiary of SinoPac Financial Holdings Company Limited since 20 June 2002, but never states ownership type. The private characterisation used in the filed Taiwan record comes only from Caproasia, a trade publication, which calls the planned Bank SinoPac / King's Town Bank combination 'the 5th largest privately-owned bank in Taiwan' and says SinoPac Financial Holdings was founded in 2002 by the Ho family as part of the Yuen Foong Yu Group. The record is filed with that attribution made explicit in its summary.
next_step: SinoPac Financial Holdings' own annual report, major-shareholders table, to replace the trade-publication citation with a primary one.

outcome: His career does cross into the private side, but the page withholds the characterisation. It says he left the Central Bank of Kuwait in 2006 to head 'an investment company in Kuwait', returned to the CBK late in 2006, served on the Capital Markets Authority Board of Commissioners from early 2012 to 2014, worked 2015-2017 for a GCC-based multi-commodities centre firm, was Vice Chairman of 'a Kuwaiti bank' from 2016 to 2018 and an independent director of 'an investment company in Kuwait' from 2017 to 2018, then President of the Kuwait Financial Intelligence Unit, Chairman of Ci-Net 2019-2020, and Governor and Chairman of the Board since April 2022. Not filed: the page never calls the bank commercial or private, and Kuwait has state-linked investment companies, so 'an investment company in Kuwait' does not settle the side. Contrast with the Deputy Governor's page, which does say 'a large commercial bank in Kuwait' - that one is filed.
next_step: A Central Bank of Kuwait press release or Kuwaiti press report naming the bank where he was Vice Chairman 2016-2018 and the investment companies, which would allow their ownership to be checked. The CBK announcement of his April 2022 appointment is the likely document.
